object_description: four-storey bar along the street with two incisions, over a transverse buried gymnasium
design_condition: the bar accompanies the street while the transverse buried gymnasium creates a casual single-storey setting towards the planned park, clearly separating public open space from the school grounds

positive: The transverse buried gymnasium creates a casual single-storey setting towards the planned park
The composition clearly separates the public open space from the school grounds
Two incisions divide the structure and refer precisely to the internal organisation
The facade is naturally greened in this area
The building has an appropriate architectural expression and the timber cladding is not too prominent here
Two clearly visible entrances provide the address from the city
The two-storey stairwells are well lit, well proportioned and clearly laid out
The kindergarten outdoor space on the gymnasium roof is also accessed from outside via an arbor-like tree canopy
The elevated jump to the all-weather pitch is designed as a stepped area
Break and sports areas are screened off by a shrub and tree filter
The project is well developed and the spatial structure defined
The two staircases are accessed directly from the entrance hall and give access to three clusters per floor
The gymnasium is structurally part of the whole but can be operated separately
The clearly laid out, efficient system requires only one lift
The simple system allows great planning and operational flexibility
The basic structure is plausible with expected medium construction costs
negative: The facility occupies the entire perimeter length, so extension is only possible by adding a storey to the gymnasium
A real replacement would have to be found for the kindergarten outdoor space
The spatial structure is still too schematic
Facade greening is mentioned in the text but only partially visible in the plans
Canteen and multi-purpose room are connected to the entrance hall but not as the desired coherent spatial unit
